experiments.name: Blot-and-plunge vitrification of protein cryo-EM grids in a Vitrobot Mark IV (4 °C, 100% RH, liquid ethane cooled by liquid nitrogen)
experiments.plain_name: Flash-freeze purified protein on a grid in liquid ethane
experiments.description: A 3 mm EM grid carrying a few microlitres of purified protein is blotted inside a humidity- and temperature-controlled chamber (4 °C, 100% relative humidity) and plunged into liquid ethane held in a liquid-nitrogen-cooled cup, producing a vitreous ice film for single-particle cryo-EM.

requirements.rationale: The environmental chamber is held at 100% relative humidity so the thin sample film does not evaporate before plunging.
requirements.document_title: Zhang Y, Nandy B, Sader K, Russo CJ, Löwe J (2025). Foam film vitrification for cryo-EM. Nature Communications. doi:10.1038/s41467-025-61270-7
requirements.location: Methods, 'Preparation of biological specimens for cryo-EM single particle analysis'
requirements.quote: For specimens prepared using the Vitrobot, all experiments were conducted with a Vitrobot Mark IV plunger set at 4 °C and 100% humidity.

requirements.rationale: Chamber set point 4 °C (277.15 K) during blotting; the NCCAT SOP lists 4-22 °C as typical, 4 °C is the reported operating point in both papers.
requirements.document_title: Gemin O, Gluc M, Rosa H, et al. (2024). Ribosomes hibernate on mitochondria during cellular stress. Nature Communications. doi:10.1038/s41467-024-52911-4
requirements.quote: blotted for 10 s with blot force + 7 before plunge-freezing in liquid ethane using a Vitrobot Mark IV (ThermoScientific) with the environmental chamber set to 4 °C and 100% humidity.

requirements.rationale: Vitrification requires plunging into liquid ethane, the rapid cryogen held in the brass cup.
requirements.document_title: Common Vitrobot Standard Operating Procedure, version 1.2 (MBSOP_VBOT_1020_1-2), Hecksel, Mulligan, Zimanyi; NCCAT CryoEM Merit Badges
requirements.location: Section 4.2 'Cooling the Ethane', safety note, page 2 of 4
requirements.quote: Liquid ethane is a rapid cryogen and can burn and cause damage to your skin and eyes.

requirements.rationale: The ethane cup is cooled by liquid nitrogen in the foam base, and finished grids go into liquid-nitrogen storage.
requirements.document_title: Common Vitrobot Standard Operating Procedure, version 1.2 (MBSOP_VBOT_1020_1-2), Hecksel, Mulligan, Zimanyi; NCCAT CryoEM Merit Badges
requirements.quote: 4.2.2. Fill outer ring of foam base with liquid nitrogen.

requirements.rationale: The specimen carrier is a standard 3 mm EM grid held in the plunger tweezers.
requirements.document_title: Zhang Y, Nandy B, Sader K, Russo CJ, Löwe J (2025). Foam film vitrification for cryo-EM. Nature Communications. doi:10.1038/s41467-025-61270-7
requirements.quote: This ensures adequate space in the centre of the loop for transferring the foam film to a standard EM grid of 3 mm diameter.

experiments.name: Single-particle cryo-EM data collection on vitrified 3 mm grids in a Titan Krios at 300 kV with the specimen held near 80 K in vacuum
experiments.plain_name: Photograph frozen protein molecules with a 300 kV electron microscope
experiments.description: Autoloaded, vitrified 3 mm grids are imaged in a Titan Krios cryo-TEM operated at 300 kV with a direct electron detector; the specimen is kept at about 80 K inside the microscope vacuum to preserve vitreous ice and limit radiation damage.

requirements.rationale: The specimen is imaged at about 80 K to keep the ice vitreous.
requirements.document_title: Dickerson JL, Leahy E, Peet MJ, Naydenova K, Russo CJ (2024). Accurate magnification determination for cryoEM using gold. Ultramicroscopy. doi:10.1016/j.ultramic.2023.113883
requirements.quote: The temperature of the specimen was ≈ 80K.

requirements.rationale: Electron imaging requires the specimen to be presented in vacuum.
requirements.document_title: Zhang Y, Nandy B, Sader K, Russo CJ, Löwe J (2025). Foam film vitrification for cryo-EM. Nature Communications. doi:10.1038/s41467-025-61270-7
requirements.quote: Because of the strong interaction of electrons with matter, the molecules of interest must be presented in vacuum and in a thin film of vitrified ice, to enable imaging by electrons and to avoid crystalline ice

requirements.rationale: The specimen is a standard 3 mm EM grid (clipped into an AutoGrid for the autoloader).
requirements.document_title: Zhang Y, Nandy B, Sader K, Russo CJ, Löwe J (2025). Foam film vitrification for cryo-EM. Nature Communications. doi:10.1038/s41467-025-61270-7
requirements.quote: This ensures adequate space in the centre of the loop for transferring the foam film to a standard EM grid of 3 mm diameter.

requirements.rationale: Vitrified grids are kept in liquid nitrogen until they are loaded into the microscope.
requirements.document_title: Dickerson JL, Leahy E, Peet MJ, Naydenova K, Russo CJ (2024). Accurate magnification determination for cryoEM using gold. Ultramicroscopy. doi:10.1016/j.ultramic.2023.113883
requirements.quote: All samples were stored in liquid nitrogen until imaging in the electron microscope.

experiments.name: High-pressure freezing (2100 bar, pressurized liquid nitrogen) of cultured neurons on 6 mm sapphire disks in a Leica HPM100 / EM ICE (flash-and-freeze)
experiments.plain_name: Freeze living brain cells under high pressure to stop them mid-signal
experiments.description: Neurons grown on 6 mm sapphire disks are sandwiched with spacer rings and frozen within milliseconds by pressurized liquid nitrogen at about 2100 bar, which vitrifies specimens up to about 200 um thick; in the flash-and-freeze variant a light pulse stimulates the cells just before freezing.

requirements.rationale: Vitrification of thick specimens relies on freezing at 2100 bar (210 MPa).
requirements.document_title: Watanabe S (2016). Flash-and-Freeze: Coordinating Optogenetic Stimulation with Rapid Freezing to Visualize Membrane Dynamics at Synapses with Millisecond Resolution. Frontiers in Synaptic Neuroscience. doi:10.3389/fnsyn.2016.00024
requirements.quote: Under high pressure (2100 bar), however, a freezing rate of 100 K/s is sufficient to freeze water in an unordered state due to the supercooling effect

requirements.rationale: Freezing is done by pressurized liquid nitrogen applied to both sides of the specimen.
requirements.document_title: Watanabe S (2016). Flash-and-Freeze: Coordinating Optogenetic Stimulation with Rapid Freezing to Visualize Membrane Dynamics at Synapses with Millisecond Resolution. Frontiers in Synaptic Neuroscience. doi:10.3389/fnsyn.2016.00024
requirements.quote: For the HPM 100 and the EM ICE, pressurized liquid nitrogen is applied to the specimen from both sides.

requirements.rationale: Cells are cultured on 6 mm sapphire disks that must fit the freezer's specimen carrier.
requirements.document_title: Watanabe S (2016). Flash-and-Freeze: Coordinating Optogenetic Stimulation with Rapid Freezing to Visualize Membrane Dynamics at Synapses with Millisecond Resolution. Frontiers in Synaptic Neuroscience. doi:10.3389/fnsyn.2016.00024
requirements.quote: On the other hand, sapphire disks as large as 6 mm can be loaded into the HPM100 or the EM ICE.

requirements.rationale: Specimens up to 200 um thick can be vitrified; the carrier stack must accommodate that thickness.
requirements.document_title: Watanabe S (2016). Flash-and-Freeze: Coordinating Optogenetic Stimulation with Rapid Freezing to Visualize Membrane Dynamics at Synapses with Millisecond Resolution. Frontiers in Synaptic Neuroscience. doi:10.3389/fnsyn.2016.00024
requirements.quote: Specimens as thick as 200 μm can be properly frozen without ice crystal formation.

requirements.rationale: Only for the flash-and-freeze variant: light stimulation must reach the specimen inside the freezer (integrated in the EM ICE).
requirements.document_title: Watanabe S (2016). Flash-and-Freeze: Coordinating Optogenetic Stimulation with Rapid Freezing to Visualize Membrane Dynamics at Synapses with Millisecond Resolution. Frontiers in Synaptic Neuroscience. doi:10.3389/fnsyn.2016.00024
requirements.quote: On the contrary EM ICE does not require a custom device or an external light source—everything is integrated.

sources.citation: Watanabe S (2016). Flash-and-Freeze: Coordinating Optogenetic Stimulation with Rapid Freezing to Visualize Membrane Dynamics at Synapses with Millisecond Resolution. Frontiers in Synaptic Neuroscience. doi:10.3389/fnsyn.2016.00024

experiments.name: Automated freeze substitution of high-pressure-frozen samples in a Leica AFS2: -90 °C hold, 5 °C/h to -20 °C, 10 °C/h to 20 °C
experiments.plain_name: Slowly swap ice for solvent in frozen cells before embedding them in resin
experiments.description: High-pressure-frozen specimens on 6 mm sapphire disks are transferred into cryotubes of fixative in acetone at -90 °C and warmed under program control (-90 °C for 5-30 h, 5 °C/h to -20 °C, 12 h at -20 °C, 10 °C/h to 20 °C) so that ice is replaced by solvent before resin embedding for electron microscopy.

requirements.rationale: The programme spans -90 °C (183.15 K) to 20 °C (293.15 K).
requirements.document_title: Watanabe S (2016). Flash-and-Freeze: Coordinating Optogenetic Stimulation with Rapid Freezing to Visualize Membrane Dynamics at Synapses with Millisecond Resolution. Frontiers in Synaptic Neuroscience. doi:10.3389/fnsyn.2016.00024
requirements.quote: The following program is used for the freeze-substitution: −90°C for 5–30 h, 5°C/h to −20°C, 12 h at −20°C, 10°C/h to 20°C.

requirements.rationale: Independent protocol: chamber pre-cooled to -90 °C before samples enter the freeze-substitution medium.
requirements.document_title: Rachid R, Wendt C, de Souza W, Miranda K (2026). Optimisation of freeze substitution protocols for the examination of malaria parasite structure by volumetric electron microscopy. Journal of Microscopy. doi:10.1111/jmi.70007
requirements.quote: The chamber was pre‐cooled to −90°C and filled with absolute ethanol (CAS #64‐17‐5, Merck, Darmstadt, Germany) to enhance heat exchange.

requirements.rationale: The 6 mm middle plate / sapphire disk is released into acetone pre-cooled in the AFS chamber.
requirements.document_title: Watanabe S (2016). Flash-and-Freeze: Coordinating Optogenetic Stimulation with Rapid Freezing to Visualize Membrane Dynamics at Synapses with Millisecond Resolution. Frontiers in Synaptic Neuroscience. doi:10.3389/fnsyn.2016.00024
requirements.quote: The sapphire disk is mounted on the countersink of a 6-mm middle plate.

requirements.rationale: The fastest programmed warming step is 10 °C/h (166.67 mK/min, rounded up to 167); the unit must ramp at least this fast under control.
requirements.document_title: Watanabe S (2016). Flash-and-Freeze: Coordinating Optogenetic Stimulation with Rapid Freezing to Visualize Membrane Dynamics at Synapses with Millisecond Resolution. Frontiers in Synaptic Neuroscience. doi:10.3389/fnsyn.2016.00024
requirements.quote: The following program is used for the freeze-substitution: −90°C for 5–30 h, 5°C/h to −20°C, 12 h at −20°C, 10°C/h to 20°C.

requirements.rationale: Frozen specimens and the osmium/glutaraldehyde fixative tubes are kept and transferred under liquid nitrogen.
requirements.document_title: Watanabe S (2016). Flash-and-Freeze: Coordinating Optogenetic Stimulation with Rapid Freezing to Visualize Membrane Dynamics at Synapses with Millisecond Resolution. Frontiers in Synaptic Neuroscience. doi:10.3389/fnsyn.2016.00024
requirements.quote: The cryotubes containing fixatives are stored under liquid nitrogen to avoid the cross-reaction between osmium tetroxide and glutaraldehyde.

sources.citation: Watanabe S (2016). Flash-and-Freeze: Coordinating Optogenetic Stimulation with Rapid Freezing to Visualize Membrane Dynamics at Synapses with Millisecond Resolution. Frontiers in Synaptic Neuroscience. doi:10.3389/fnsyn.2016.00024

experiments.name: Tokuyasu cryo-ultramicrotomy of 2.3 M sucrose-infused cell pellets: trimming at -100 °C, 50-80 nm sections at -120 °C (Leica UC7/FC7)
experiments.plain_name: Cut ultra-thin frozen slices of cells for antibody gold labelling
experiments.description: Gelatin-embedded cell pellets (about 1 mm cubes) are infused with 2.3 M sucrose, frozen in liquid nitrogen on aluminium pins, trimmed at -100 °C and sectioned at -120 °C into 50-80 nm ultrathin cryosections in a cryo-ultramicrotome, then thawed for immunogold labelling and TEM.

requirements.rationale: Trimming at -100 °C and ultrathin sectioning at -120 °C.
requirements.document_title: De Mazière A, van der Beek J, van Dijk S, de Heus C, Reggiori F, Koike M, Klumperman J (2022). An optimized protocol for immuno-electron microscopy of endogenous LC3. Autophagy. doi:10.1080/15548627.2022.2056864
requirements.quote: Trimming of the blocks in preparation to thin sectioning was done at −100°C. Ultrathin sections (50–80 nm) were cut at −120°C.

requirements.rationale: Ultrathin cryosections of 50-80 nm are required.
requirements.document_title: De Mazière A, van der Beek J, van Dijk S, de Heus C, Reggiori F, Koike M, Klumperman J (2022). An optimized protocol for immuno-electron microscopy of endogenous LC3. Autophagy. doi:10.1080/15548627.2022.2056864
requirements.quote: Ultrathin sections (50–80 nm) were cut at −120°C.

requirements.rationale: Blocks are frozen and stored in liquid nitrogen before cryosectioning.
requirements.document_title: De Mazière A, van der Beek J, van Dijk S, de Heus C, Reggiori F, Koike M, Klumperman J (2022). An optimized protocol for immuno-electron microscopy of endogenous LC3. Autophagy. doi:10.1080/15548627.2022.2056864
requirements.quote: Blocks were mounted on aluminum specimen holders, frozen and stored in liquid nitrogen.

requirements.rationale: About 1 mm cubic blocks; circumscribed diameter of a 1 mm x 1 mm face is 1.414 mm (rounded up).
requirements.document_title: De Mazière A, van der Beek J, van Dijk S, de Heus C, Reggiori F, Koike M, Klumperman J (2022). An optimized protocol for immuno-electron microscopy of endogenous LC3. Autophagy. doi:10.1080/15548627.2022.2056864
requirements.quote: The cell pellets were cut to cubic blocks of ~1 mm 3 at 4°C.

experiments.name: Cryo-FIB lamella milling of vitrified yeast on AutoGrids in an Aquilos DualBeam with stage and shield at -180 °C
experiments.plain_name: Carve a thin window through a frozen cell with an ion beam
experiments.description: Plunge-frozen cells on 3 mm grids clipped into Cryo-FIB AutoGrids are coated with organometallic and sputtered platinum and milled with a 30 kV ion beam (300 to 30 pA) into lamellae thinner than 200 nm, with the stage and anti-contamination shield at -180 °C under vacuum, for subsequent cryo-electron tomography.

requirements.rationale: Stage and anti-contaminating shield held at -180 °C (93.15 K) during milling.
requirements.document_title: Gemin O, Gluc M, Rosa H, et al. (2024). Ribosomes hibernate on mitochondria during cellular stress. Nature Communications. doi:10.1038/s41467-024-52911-4
requirements.quote: The temperature of both the stage and the anti-contaminating shield were held at − 180 °C.

requirements.rationale: Ion/electron-beam milling and SEM imaging of vitrified samples take place in vacuum.
requirements.document_title: Zhang Y, Nandy B, Sader K, Russo CJ, Löwe J (2025). Foam film vitrification for cryo-EM. Nature Communications. doi:10.1038/s41467-025-61270-7
requirements.quote: Because of the strong interaction of electrons with matter, the molecules of interest must be presented in vacuum and in a thin film of vitrified ice, to enable imaging by electrons and to avoid crystalline ice

requirements.rationale: Specimens are standard 3 mm EM grids clipped into Cryo-FIB AutoGrids.
requirements.document_title: Zhang Y, Nandy B, Sader K, Russo CJ, Löwe J (2025). Foam film vitrification for cryo-EM. Nature Communications. doi:10.1038/s41467-025-61270-7
requirements.quote: This ensures adequate space in the centre of the loop for transferring the foam film to a standard EM grid of 3 mm diameter.

requirements.rationale: Grids are clipped in cold nitrogen vapour before loading; nitrogen cooling of the cryo-stage.
requirements.document_title: Gemin O, Gluc M, Rosa H, et al. (2024). Ribosomes hibernate on mitochondria during cellular stress. Nature Communications. doi:10.1038/s41467-024-52911-4
requirements.quote: Vitrified grids were clipped in CryoFIB Autogrids (ThermoScientific, ref. 1205101) in cold nitrogen vapor, then loaded in an Aquilos DualBeam cryoFIB/SEM (ThermoScientific)

experiments.name: Macromolecular X-ray diffraction data collection at 100 K on a loop-mounted, liquid-nitrogen flash-cooled protein crystal in an Oxford Cryostream
experiments.plain_name: Collect X-ray diffraction from a protein crystal kept at 100 K
experiments.description: A cryoprotected protein crystal mounted in a nylon loop is flash-cooled in liquid nitrogen and kept at 100 K in an open-flow nitrogen gas stream on the goniometer while diffraction images are recorded; cooling below the glass transition of water (about 136-155 K) limits radiation damage.

requirements.rationale: Diffraction data are collected with the crystal at 100 K.
requirements.document_title: Kumar A, Karthikeyan S (2018). Crystal structure of the MSMEG_4306 gene product from Mycobacterium smegmatis. Acta Crystallographica Section F. doi:10.1107/s2053230x18002236
requirements.location: Section 2, 'Crystallization, data collection and structure determination of MSMEG_4306'
requirements.quote: The data were collected at 100 K using an Oxford Cryostream.

requirements.rationale: The crystal must be held below the lower bound of the water glass-transition range (about 136 K).
requirements.document_title: Pflugrath JW (2015). Practical macromolecular cryocrystallography. Acta Crystallographica Section F. doi:10.1107/s2053230x15008304
requirements.quote: Flash-cooling a crystal to a temperature below the glass-transition phase (∼136–155 K; Weik, Kryger et al. , 2001 ▶ ; Weik, Ravelli et al. , 2001 ▶ ; Chinte et al. , 2005 ▶ ; see Fig. 1 ▶ ) is the method used to trap the molecules

requirements.rationale: Crystals are flash-cooled in liquid nitrogen before data collection.
requirements.document_title: Kumar A, Karthikeyan S (2018). Crystal structure of the MSMEG_4306 gene product from Mycobacterium smegmatis. Acta Crystallographica Section F. doi:10.1107/s2053230x18002236
requirements.quote: The crystals obtained were mounted on a nylon loop (Hampton Research, USA) and flash-cooled in liquid nitrogen before data collection.

experiments.name: Long-term -80 °C storage of plasmid-bearing bacteria as 25% glycerol stocks in 2 mL screw-top cryovials (Addgene protocol)
experiments.plain_name: Bank bacteria and their plasmids in a minus-80 freezer
experiments.description: 500 uL of overnight culture is mixed with 500 uL of 50% glycerol in a 2 mL screw-top cryovial, frozen and kept at -80 °C, where it stays viable for years; the stock is kept on dry ice when streaked so it does not thaw.

requirements.rationale: The stock is stored at -80 °C (193.15 K) for years.
requirements.document_title: Addgene Protocol: Creating Bacterial Glycerol Stocks for Long-term Storage of Plasmids
requirements.quote: The stock is now stable for years, as long as it is kept at -80°C.

requirements.rationale: Each stock is a 2 mL screw-top cryovial; the store must hold 2 mL cryovials.
requirements.document_title: Addgene Protocol: Creating Bacterial Glycerol Stocks for Long-term Storage of Plasmids
requirements.quote: add 500 μL of the overnight culture to 500 μL of 50% glycerol in a 2 mL screw top tube or cryovial and gently mix.

requirements.rationale: Optional handling: keep the vial on dry ice while streaking so it does not thaw.
requirements.document_title: Addgene Protocol: Creating Bacterial Glycerol Stocks for Long-term Storage of Plasmids
requirements.quote: Placing the glycerol stock on dry ice while streaking onto LB agar will prevent it from thawing completely and will improve the shelf life.

sources.citation: Addgene Protocol: Creating Bacterial Glycerol Stocks for Long-term Storage of Plasmids

experiments.name: Freeze-drying of Lactobacillus suspensions with lyoprotectant: primary drying at -40 °C, 10 Pa, condenser -55 °C; secondary drying to 25 °C (Labconco FreeZone 18 L with stoppering tray dryer)
experiments.plain_name: Freeze-dry probiotic bacteria into a shelf-stable powder
experiments.description: Lactobacillus cells resuspended in lyoprotectant are frozen at -80 °C (-2 °C/min) and freeze-dried for 24 h: 2 h at -40 °C with chamber pressure 10 Pa and condenser at -55 °C, warming at 0.04 °C/min to 0 °C, then secondary drying to 25 °C at 0.08 °C/min.

requirements.rationale: Sublimation needs an evacuated drying chamber.
requirements.document_title: Bodzen A, Jossier A, Dupont S, et al. (2021). Design of a new lyoprotectant increasing freeze-dried Lactobacillus strain survival to long-term storage. BMC Biotechnology. doi:10.1186/s12896-021-00726-2
requirements.quote: Sublimation was carried out by maintaining the samples for 2 h at -40 °C (condenser temperature = − 55 °C and chamber pressure = 10 Pa), then increasing the chamber temperature to 0 °C at a speed of 0.04 °C/min.

requirements.rationale: The chamber must reach 10 Pa or lower during primary drying.
requirements.document_title: Bodzen A, Jossier A, Dupont S, et al. (2021). Design of a new lyoprotectant increasing freeze-dried Lactobacillus strain survival to long-term storage. BMC Biotechnology. doi:10.1186/s12896-021-00726-2
requirements.quote: Sublimation was carried out by maintaining the samples for 2 h at -40 °C (condenser temperature = − 55 °C and chamber pressure = 10 Pa), then increasing the chamber temperature to 0 °C at a speed of 0.04 °C/min.

requirements.rationale: Shelf/chamber temperature runs from -40 °C (primary drying) to 25 °C (secondary desorption).
requirements.document_title: Bodzen A, Jossier A, Dupont S, et al. (2021). Design of a new lyoprotectant increasing freeze-dried Lactobacillus strain survival to long-term storage. BMC Biotechnology. doi:10.1186/s12896-021-00726-2
requirements.quote: After 17 h, the chamber temperature was increased to 25 °C at a heating rate of 0.08 °C/min to carry out the secondary desorption.

requirements.rationale: Condenser must reach -55 °C (218.15 K) or colder.
requirements.document_title: Bodzen A, Jossier A, Dupont S, et al. (2021). Design of a new lyoprotectant increasing freeze-dried Lactobacillus strain survival to long-term storage. BMC Biotechnology. doi:10.1186/s12896-021-00726-2
requirements.quote: Sublimation was carried out by maintaining the samples for 2 h at -40 °C (condenser temperature = − 55 °C and chamber pressure = 10 Pa), then increasing the chamber temperature to 0 °C at a speed of 0.04 °C/min.

requirements.rationale: Controlled shelf warming at 0.08 °C/min (80 mK/min) during secondary drying.
requirements.document_title: Bodzen A, Jossier A, Dupont S, et al. (2021). Design of a new lyoprotectant increasing freeze-dried Lactobacillus strain survival to long-term storage. BMC Biotechnology. doi:10.1186/s12896-021-00726-2
requirements.quote: After 17 h, the chamber temperature was increased to 25 °C at a heating rate of 0.08 °C/min to carry out the secondary desorption.

experiments.name: Cryogenic impact grinding of cartilage tissue for total-RNA extraction in a SPEX large Freezer/Mill (vials immersed in liquid nitrogen, about -196 °C)
experiments.plain_name: Grind frozen cartilage into powder for RNA extraction
experiments.description: Cartilage samples sealed in grinding vials with a magnetically driven impactor are pre-cooled and pulverized while immersed in liquid nitrogen (held at about -196 °C), up to four samples at once with the multi-vial adapter, keeping tissue far below -80 °C so RNA is not degraded.

requirements.rationale: Samples are held at about -196 °C (77.15 K) in the liquid-nitrogen bath during pre-cooling and grinding.
requirements.document_title: SPEX SamplePrep 14th Edition Handbook: Freezer/Mill section and application notes
requirements.quote: By utilizing the precool function of the Freezer/Mill, the samples were held at about -196 °C for another two minutes.

requirements.rationale: Tissue for RNA or protein extraction must stay at -80 °C or colder throughout.
requirements.document_title: SPEX SamplePrep 14th Edition Handbook: Freezer/Mill section and application notes
requirements.location: 'Using the Freezer/Mill for cryogenic grinding of plant and animal tissue', handbook page 65
requirements.quote: Samples that require extraction of RNA or proteins must be kept at -80º C or lower during the entire extraction process.

requirements.rationale: Grinding vials are immersed in liquid nitrogen throughout the grinding cycle.
requirements.document_title: SPEX SamplePrep 14th Edition Handbook: Freezer/Mill section and application notes
requirements.quote: The sample is hermetically sealed in the grinding vial and immersed in liquid nitrogen, so cross contamination is eliminated.

sources.citation: SPEX SamplePrep 14th Edition Handbook: Freezer/Mill section and application notes
